elections.notes: Republican primary runoff for Governor (Toby Doeden vs. incumbent Larry Rhoden), required because no candidate received 35% in the June 2, 2026 primary; absentee voting began June 12, 2026.
Advance in-person voting may begin July 15 (varies by county) and must begin in all counties by July 28; it ends at 12:00 noon on August 3.

Registration deadline is for mail/online; in-person registration with proof of residency continues through Election Day. Secretary of State and Attorney General nominees are chosen at party conventions, not in this primary; the primary nominates for U.S. Senate, Governor, U.S. House, and the Legislature.
Primary nominates for all 8 U.S. House districts, State Auditor (the only statewide office up in 2026), and the Legislature; no U.S. Senate or Governor race in Missouri in 2026.

Virginia's 2026 primary, originally set for June 16, was moved to August 4, 2026 per an official Department of Elections news release; primaries are held only for offices/parties with contested nominations.

Top-two primary; ballot includes U.S. Representative, State Senator/Representative, and statewide judicial (Supreme Court, Court of Appeals) — no U.S. Senate or Governor race in 2026 and no statewide executive offices; all-mail voting with ballots mailed by July 17, so no traditional early-voting period; registration deadline is online/mail, in-person through Election Day.
State primary (held concurrently with county general elections) nominating candidates for the Nov. 3 general.
Same-day voter registration available; all-mail election with in-person voting at voter service centers (excluding Sundays).
Same-day voter registration available.
Same-day voter registration available.
Same-day voter registration available.
Same-day voter registration available.
Top-four nonpartisan open primary; top four advance to the ranked-choice general election.
Closed primary; early-voting dates shown are the mandatory statewide period (counties may offer additional days). Per DOS, no special U.S. Senate primary is held on this date.
Same-day voter registration available (register and vote at the polls); advance registration closed August 3, 2026.
Runoff applies only to races in which no candidate received a majority in the June 16, 2026 primary.
Same-day voter registration available.
Primary held on a Wednesday; RI Department of State confirms the new 2026 primary date of September 9 due to the Labor Day holiday.
Closed primary; early-voting sites closed Sunday Sept. 6 and Labor Day Sept. 7 within the listed window.
General election uses ranked-choice voting among top-four primary finishers.
Statewide primary was held May 19, 2026, with runoffs in June; Alabama has no early in-person voting; Governor (Ivey term-limited) and the Class 2 U.S. Senate seat are both on the ballot.
A General Runoff Election, if required for eligible (e.g., nonpartisan/municipal) races, is set for December 1, 2026.
No U.S. Senate seat is up in Arizona in 2026; Governor and all other statewide executive offices plus all 9 U.S. House districts and the Legislature are on the ballot.
All active registered voters are mailed ballots beginning 2026-10-05; same-day (conditional) voter registration available after the deadline; no U.S. Senate seat on California's 2026 ballot.
All-mail voting state; every voter receives a mail ballot; same-day voter registration available in person through Election Day.
Same-day voter registration available.
Same-day voter registration available.
Early-voting sites closed Sunday Oct. 25 within the listed window; Delaware has no 2026 governor's race (next in 2028).
Includes special U.S. Senate election for the remainder of the unexpired term (appointee Ashley Moody's seat); early-voting dates shown are the mandatory statewide period.
Governor's race is open (Kemp term-limited) and the Class 2 U.S. Senate seat is up; May 19 primary and June 16 primary runoff were held before July 25.
Same-day voter registration available; early-voting dates are voter service center in-person voting through Election Day (excluding Sundays).
Same-day voter registration available (pre-registration deadline is 5:00 p.m. Monday, October 19, 2026); early voting shown is in-person absentee at the county auditor's office.
Same-day voter registration available at the polls on Election Day; early in-person voting offered only in counties that choose to conduct it.

Open U.S. Senate seat (Sen. Dick Durbin not seeking re-election) plus Governor, all 17 U.S. House districts, statewide constitutional officers, and the General Assembly; early voting begins Sept 24 at election-authority main sites, with additional permanent sites opening later (e.g., Oct 19 in some jurisdictions).

No U.S. Senate seat and no Governor's race in Indiana in 2026; ballot includes all 9 U.S. House districts, statewide offices (Secretary of State, Auditor/Comptroller, Treasurer), and the Legislature; early (in-person absentee) voting ends at 12:00 noon on Nov 2.

U.S. Senate Class II seat (incumbent Roger Marshall) and an open Governor's race (Gov. Kelly term-limited) are both on the 2026 ballot; advance in-person voting may begin Oct 14, must begin in all counties by Oct 27, and ends at 12:00 noon Nov 2.
Early voting shown is Kentucky's three-day no-excuse in-person absentee period; state legislative seats also on the ballot (no statewide constitutional offices in 2026).

Officially titled 'U.S. Senate General/Open U.S. Representative Primary/Open Primary Election': the U.S. Senate race is the party-general round (closed party primaries for U.S. Senate, La. Supreme Court, PSC and BESE were held May 16, 2026), while U.S. House and other open-primary offices hold their open (jungle) primary this day; online (GeauxVote) registration deadline is Oct 13; early voting excludes Sunday, Oct 25.
Same-day voter registration available.
Same-day voter registration available; Maine's statewide primary was held June 9, 2026.

Open U.S. Senate seat (Sen. Gary Peters not seeking re-election) and open Governor's race (Gov. Whitmer term-limited); registration deadline is mail/online, with in-person registration through Nov 3; Oct 24-Nov 1 is the constitutionally mandated minimum early voting period and some jurisdictions offer additional days.
Same-day voter registration available.
No U.S. Senate or Governor race in Missouri in 2026; State Auditor is the only statewide executive office on the ballot, alongside all 8 U.S. House seats and the Legislature.

Ballot also includes nonpartisan judicial races (Supreme Court, Court of Appeals, trial courts); no governor or legislature in 2026 (odd-year offices); Mississippi has no standard early in-person voting (in-person absentee only). The statewide primary and runoff were held in June 2026.
No Governor race in 2026 (Montana elects its governor in presidential years); late voter registration available until noon on Election Day.

No 2026 governor's race; statewide contests are judicial (e.g., N.C. Supreme Court / Court of Appeals) plus all General Assembly seats; the statewide primary was held March 3, 2026; same-day registration is available during early voting; early voting ends 3 p.m. Oct 31.
North Dakota has no voter registration requirement; no U.S. Senate or Governor race in 2026.
Class II U.S. Senate seat and Governor both on the 2026 ballot; Secretary of State, Attorney General, Treasurer and Auditor also up.
Same-day voter registration available.
No governor or state legislative races in 2026 (those are odd-year elections in New Jersey); the statewide primary was held June 2, 2026.
Same-day voter registration available during early voting and on Election Day.
Active registered voters receive mail ballots; same-day voter registration available; no U.S. Senate seat on Nevada's 2026 ballot.
No U.S. Senate seat up in 2026; the statewide primary was held June 23, 2026.

The U.S. Senate race is a SPECIAL election for the seat vacated by JD Vance and filled by appointee Jon Husted (no regular Ohio Senate seat is up in 2026); Governor's race is open (Gov. DeWine term-limited).
All-mail voting state; ballots mailed to registered voters beginning 2026-10-14.
No traditional early in-person voting in PA (mail ballot application deadline is 5:00 p.m. October 27, 2026); Lieutenant Governor and state legislative seats also on the ballot.

Early voting runs daily 8:30 a.m.-6 p.m., closed Sunday during the period; statewide primaries were held June 9, 2026 (runoffs two weeks later); open governor's race (McMaster term-limited) and the Class 2 U.S. Senate seat are on the ballot.
No same-day registration; absentee voting (including in person) begins September 18, 2026.
The statewide primary was held March 3, 2026 (runoff in May); U.S. Senate seat (Class 2) and Governor are both on the 2026 ballot.
All-mail voting state; ballots mailed to registered voters; same-day voter registration available (in person with two forms of ID); no Governor or U.S. Senate race in Utah in 2026.

No governor or General Assembly races in 2026 (odd-year offices); a district-level House of Delegates District 20 special election also appears on the Nov 3 ballot; same-day registration with a provisional ballot is available through Election Day.
Same-day voter registration available.

No U.S. Senate seat and no Governor's race in Washington in 2026; ballot has all 10 U.S. House districts, the Legislature, and statewide judicial offices; all-mail voting state (no traditional early-voting window); registration deadline is online/mail, with in-person registration through Election Day Nov 3.
Same-day voter registration available.
State legislative seats also on the ballot; no Governor race in 2026 (next in 2028).
Same-day voter registration available (register and vote at the polls); advance registration closes October 19, 2026.

Held only for Nov 3 races in which no candidate receives the required majority (Georgia requires a majority to win the general election); voters must have been registered by the Oct 5, 2026 general-election deadline.

Listed on the official calendar as 'General/Special Runoff Election Day'; held only for races (e.g., nonpartisan judicial contests or special elections) in which no candidate wins the required majority on November 3.

Officially the 'Open General Election' — held only for races in which no candidate wins the required majority on Nov 3 (U.S. House districts without a majority winner, plus open-primary judicial/local races); online (GeauxVote) registration deadline Nov 21; early voting excludes Sunday, Nov 29.
